Instrument: Levenson MR, Jennings PA, Aldwin CM, Shiraishi RW (2005) Int J Aging Hum Dev 60(2):127-43.
note: Clean pass; mapping proven against the paper's own published correlation matrix. INSTRUMENT (Step 3b): the table name 'sti' is correct -- the live 10 items STI1..STI10 are the 10-item self-transcendence scale of Levenson, Jennings, Aldwin & Shiraishi's Adult Self-Transcendence Inventory (ASTI), cited as ref [33] in Monier et al. (2026) PLOS ONE 21(7):e0352176 ('we used (5) the Self-transcendence Inventory [33] composed of 10 items'). The S1 Table's other blocks (PoT judgments, BDI, STAI, FFMQ, happiness questionnaires) are separate columns and separate IRW tables; only the STI block is here. WORDS: the paper's Table 6 (10.1371/journal.pone.0352176.t006) prints all 10 items in full, numbered 1-10, as row labels of the item-level correlation matrix. That table is an IMAGE -- grep over the scraped article text returns nothing -- so it was read from the PNG at journals.plos.org/plosone/article/figure/image?size=large&id=10.1371/journal.pone.0352176.t006 and transcribed by eye; a human spot-check of punctuation is worth one minute. Transcribed literally: item 8 ends WITHOUT a full stop in the source and ships that way, and item 3's published English is 'I do not become angry as easily' (the ASTI's own 25-item present-tense form reads 'I do not become angry easily') -- nothing was normalised toward canonical ASTI wording. LANGUAGE: the study is French (Clermont-Ferrand, French ethics committee) and the S1 Table's STI column headers are French. No full French wording is published anywhere in the deposit or the paper -- the headers carry only truncated CamelCase fragments (STI2_esChosesMaterielles, STI5_eRessensBeaucoupPlus are cut on the LEFT; STI7_IlEstPlusFacilede and STI9_JeSensDavantage stop mid-sentence), and S1 Table is the article's only Supporting Information file. So the paper's English ships in the base fields with language=French and no _translated columns -- the documented fallback, same call as the sibling monier_2026_pot in batch_109. ANCHORS: the paper states the 7-point anchors for its PoT questions and its happiness questionnaires but says nothing at all about the STI response scale (the live data run 1-7; the ASTI's canonical form is 1-4, so canonical anchors would have been wrong as well as unsourced). option_text therefore ships blank for all of resp 1-7 rather than padded with the numbers themselves, and instructions/section_prompt are NA for the same reason -- no administered instruction text is recoverable. MAPPING: recorded paper_explicit rather than data_labels because the shipped WORDS come from the paper's numbering, not from the headers (the headers hold fragments, not items). It is nevertheless verified end to end, not inferred: all 70 cells of Table 6 recompute from the S1 Table columns to within 0.0054 (printed to 2 dp), each S1 column's nearest published row is its own with a 14x-48x margin over the best wrong row, and per-item n from irw_table_sets() matches the raw column counts 10/10 (101/105/105/104/104/104/103/104/104/105). See verify_monier_2026_sti.R. The French header fragments independently agree with all 10 English items (STI6_JeTrouvePlusdeJoieDansLaVie / 'I find more joy in life'; STI10_JeMinquieteMoins / 'I have become less concerned about other people's opinions of me'). RIGHTS: no restriction locatable for the ASTI and so nothing to quote -- there is no ASTI/Levenson row in instrument_rights_register.csv, no publisher sells it (it was published in a journal article, Int J Aging Hum Dev 2005;60(2):127-43), its items are reproduced openly in the CRAN package MPsychoR's ASTI help page and in this CC BY 4.0 PLOS article, and searches surfaced no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause from Levenson or any rights holder. Silence is permission, so the rights rule does not fire. A register row for the ASTI would be a reasonable add for a later pass.
public_note: Item text for this table is the English wording printed in the study's own Table 6; the inventory was administered in French, and no full French original is published in the paper or its S1 Table, so the administered wording could not be shipped. The paper never states the 7-point response anchors, so option text is blank.

public_note: The ERQ was administered in Spanish (the Cabello et al., 2013 adaptation) to a mostly Chilean sample, but neither the PeerJ deposit nor the paper's supplement contains any Spanish item wording -- the deposit's ERQ columns are bare codes ERQ_1..ERQ_10 -- so the item text shown here is Gross and John's (2003) canonical English ERQ rather than the sentences participants read. Item codes erq1-erq10 follow the instrument's printed item numbers; the split into reappraisal (erq1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10) and suppression (erq2, 4, 6, 9) wording is confirmed by the paper's Table S.5, whose twelve published subscale statistics reproduce exactly under that key and under no other of the 210 possible six-item splits, but nothing in the data distinguishes the near-parallel reappraisal items 1, 3, 7 and 10 from one another. Scale points 2, 3, 5 and 6 carry no option text because the ERQ form labels only 1, 4 and 7.

public_note: The items of `motion` are stimulus conditions in a random-dot motion task, not questions: each item code is block number and motion coherence (e.g. '1 6' = block 1, 6% coherence), and the item_text IRW ships is a description of that stimulus rather than wording the child read.
